item.title: Evaluating Typographic Detail
item.description: Review the proof for Lines Across Water, an illustrated monograph on ferry terminals, and describe how type design and page composition affect the finished pages. The production team uses widow for the last line of a paragraph stranded at the top of the next page or column.

children.definition: Adjustment of the horizontal space between a specific pair of glyphs to correct an apparent gap or collision.
children.example: The kerning between the W and A in WATER needs tightening because their diagonal strokes leave a conspicuous gap.
children.translation_uz: kerning (muayyan belgilar jufti orasidagi masofani sozlash)

children.definition: The vertical distance from the baseline of one line of type to the baseline of the next.
children.example: Increase the leading in the ferry schedules so the eye can follow each row of departure times across the spread.

children.definition: A consistent increase or decrease in interletter spacing across a selected span of text.
children.example: Loosen the tracking across the entire chapter heading so the spaced capitals in NIGHT CROSSINGS feel less cramped.
children.translation_uz: treking (matn boʻlagi boʻylab harflar oraligʻini bir xil miqdorda oʻzgartirish)

children.definition: Positioning typographic elements according to their perceived edges or centers so they appear to line up.
children.example: For optical alignment, let the opening quotation mark on the dockworker’s statement hang just beyond the left edge of the column.

children.definition: The overall impression of lightness or darkness in a block of type, produced by the distribution of strokes and white space.
children.example: The typographic color of the route histories is uneven in the proof because patches of tight spacing alternate with broad gaps between words.

children.definition: A single glyph that represents a sequence of two or more characters, often with their forms joined.
children.example: In the heading ‘The first crossing’, use the fi ligature in ‘first’ to keep the hook of the f from crowding the dot of the i.
children.translation_uz: ligatura (ikki yoki undan ortiq belgini ifodalovchi yagona glif)

children.definition: Under this production team's convention, the last line of a paragraph carried over on its own to the top of the next page or column.
children.example: The paragraph about the last steam ferry leaves a widow at the top of page 47, so reflow the text to carry two lines over together.
children.translation_ru: последняя строка абзаца, оставшаяся одна в начале следующей страницы или колонки
children.translation_uz: xatboshining keyingi sahifa yoki ustun boshida yolgʻiz qolgan oxirgi satri

children.definition: The uneven outline formed by the ends of lines at the unaligned edge of a text block.
children.example: The right-hand rag of the terminal captions has a deep notch where three short lines fall together.
children.translation_uz: matn satrlari uchlari hosil qilgan notekis chet

children.definition: The distance from the baseline to the top of a typeface’s lowercase x, used as a measure of the height of its main lowercase forms.
children.example: At the same point size, the face with the larger x-height makes the lowercase words in the terminal captions look bigger.
children.translation_uz: kichik x harfining tayanch chizigʻidan tepasigacha boʻlgan balandligi

children.definition: An area of negative space wholly or partly enclosed by the strokes of a glyph.
children.example: On the uncoated proof, ink spread has nearly filled the counter of the lowercase e in the smallest ferry captions.
children.translation_uz: belgi chiziqlari toʻliq yoki qisman oʻrab turgan boʻshliq

children.definition: The slight extension of a rounded or pointed glyph beyond a horizontal reference line so it appears to align with glyphs whose flat edges meet that line.
children.example: The capital O in the title lettering has enough overshoot below the baseline to look level with the flat-footed L beside it.
children.translation_uz: belgilar koʻzga bir tekis koʻrinishi uchun yumaloq yoki uchli qismning gorizontal moʻljal chizigʻidan biroz chiqib turishi

children.definition: Capital-shaped forms drawn at a reduced height, usually near the lowercase height, with proportions and stroke weights designed to match the surrounding type.
children.example: Set the ferry names in small caps so their capital forms sit comfortably beside lowercase text in the route notes.
children.translation_uz: kichik harflar boʻyiga yaqin qilib maxsus chizilgan bosh harf shakllari

children.definition: The system of visual distinctions in type that signals the relative importance and relationships of text elements.
children.example: The typographic hierarchy on the opening spread should make the chapter title register first, the terminal name second, and the construction date third.

children.definition: Short lines printed outside the finished page area to indicate where the sheet should be cut.
children.example: Use the crop marks to locate the trim line, then check that the ferry-ramp photograph extends at least 3 mm beyond it.
children.translation_uz: bosma varaqni qayerdan kesish kerakligini koʻrsatuvchi belgilar
